answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by gating earning power behind earned, time-locked reputation: a new identity starts with zero weight and must complete small, independently verifiable useful tasks before its votes or claims count. Like shale laid down layer by layer, reputation accrues slowly and cannot be bought in bulk; a comet-fast flood of fresh identities arrives weightless. At dawn of each epoch, only identities whose work history predates the round may earn, so cloning an agent a thousand times costs a thousand times the work.
